articles.title: New Zealand card spending falls for second month as food prices hold flat in September
articles.desc: The data adds to a mixed picture for the New Zealand dollar, with weak household spending offsetting the stronger manufacturing survey released earlier in the day. A second monthly fall in card spending points to soft domestic demand, which tends to argue against tighter policy, while flat food pric
articles.content: The data adds to a mixed picture for the New Zealand dollar, with weak household spending offsetting the stronger manufacturing survey released earlier in the day. A second monthly fall in card spending points to soft domestic demand, which tends to argue against tighter policy, while flat food prices remove one source of upward pressure on inflation for the month. Fuel costs, which manufacturers flagged as a key concern, remain the bigger swing factor for household budgets, leaving oil prices important for the consumer outlook. --- Yesterday: RBNZ’s Conway says October rate decision completely open, OCR more likely to rise --- New Zealand’s factories are finding their stride, but its shoppers are still keeping their cards in their wallets, and flat food prices are only a modest consolation. Summary: Seasonally adjusted electronic card retail spending fell 0.4% in September, after a 0.9% drop in August Actual card spending rose 0.9% from a year earlier, up from 0.2% in August Card data covers about 68% of core retail sales Food prices were unchanged on the month, after a 0.3% rise in August, and up 2.4% on the year Food accounts for nearly 19% of the consumers price index The weak consumer data contrasts with a strong manufacturing PMI released the same day New Zealand electronic card retail spending fell for a second straight month in September, while food prices held steady, according to data from Statistics New Zealand on Friday. The figures point to cautious households even as other parts of the economy show more life. Seasonally adjusted retail spending on electronic cards slipped 0.4% from August, following a 0.9% decline the previous month. In unadjusted terms, actual spending was 0.9% higher than in September last year, a firmer annual pace than the 0.2% recorded in August. Electronic card transactions cover roughly 68% of core retail sales and are the main monthly gauge of retail activity in New Zealand. The figures suggest consumers remain under pressure. Back-to-back monthly declines in spending, after seasonal adjustment, point to households trimming discretionary purchases, while the annual rise in actual spending is modest. Because the card data measures the value of transactions rather than volumes, part of that rise reflects higher prices. Separately, Statistics New Zealand’s food price index was unchanged in September from August, after a 0.3% rise the month before. Food prices were 2.4% higher than a year earlier. Food carries a weight of nearly 19% in the consumers price index, so a flat monthly reading removes one source of upward pressure on headline inflation for the month. The softer consumer data contrasts with a stronger picture from manufacturers. The BNZ-BusinessNZ manufacturing index released earlier on Friday showed the sector expanding at a much stronger rate in September. However, many firms cited fuel prices, cost of living pressures and uncertainty ahead of the election as concerns. Taken together, the releases describe an economy where production and orders are picking up but household spending is lagging, held back by living costs. A pause in food price growth offers some relief. On its own, however, it is unlikely to change the broader picture for household budgets while fuel costs stay elevated. The next indications of consumer strength will come from upcoming retail and inflation data. They will show whether September’s weakness in card spending persists into the final quarter, when pre-Christmas demand typically provides a seasonal lift. This article was written by Eamonn Sheridan at investinglive.com.

articles.title: Big Walk Skips Xbox as House House Takes a Stand Against Microsoft
articles.desc: Big Walk will skip Xbox while Microsoft remains a target of the BDS boycott. Find out why House House made this choice and how it may affect players.
articles.content: Big Walk Skips Xbox as House House Takes a Stand Against Microsoft Big Walk Skips Xbox as House House Takes a Stand Against Microsoft Big Walk developer House House has ruled out an Xbox release in support of the BDS boycott of Microsoft. The move could stop some friends from playing the co-op game together. Big Walk will not come to Xbox while Microsoft remains a target of the Boycott, Divestment, Sanctions (BDS) movement. For those who are still unaware of the BDS movement, this campaign calls for boycotts of companies that are believed to be in support of Israel’s actions against Palestinians. Microsoft has faced criticism over its work with the Israeli government and military. Developer House House said it would consider an Xbox release only if Microsoft and/or Xbox are removed from the BDS boycott list. According to the official statement, “We would love for people to be able to play the game on Xbox, but not until Microsoft and/or Xbox have been removed as BDS boycott targets.” It further stated, “We’ve made this decision with the belief that meaningful change can be made in the world, that coordinated collective action can confront even the most powerful interests, and that one day, Palestine will be free.” The game is planned for PC, PlayStation 5, and Nintendo Switch 2. House House knows that skipping Xbox could leave some players out. In its statement, the studio said it understood that some people would be upset because they could not play with friends on other systems. Still, it believes that taking a stand can help push large companies to change. The studio has not shared a date for a possible Xbox release. Microsoft’s Xbox Labs to Test Emerging Gaming Ideas and Technology How Platform Choice Can Split Gaming Groups Big Walk is a co-op game where players explore, solve puzzles, and work together. Playing a co-op game with friends has always been one of the most enjoyable experiences, but friends do not always own the same console or gaming PC. Here comes the importance of cross-platform play, which can help players join the same game, even when they use different systems. However, that only works if the game is available on their platform. When one version is missing, some friends may need to buy new hardware, which can be costly. Others may have to pick a different game. House House’s decision puts its beliefs ahead of reaching every Xbox player. For now, those who want to play Big Walk will need to use one of its planned platforms other than Xbox. to get the latest news, exclusives and videos on WhatsApp NBA 2K27 on Xbox Play Anywhere: Buy Once, Play on Console and PC GTA 6 Still Has No PC Release: Xbox’s GTA 6 Cloud Gaming Surprise Falls Apart Microsoft Brings Disc-to-Digital Feature to All Xbox Users Microsoft Moves Halo Development to Activision After Halo Studios Layoffs

articles.title: Rocket Lab pushes back first Neutron launch to 2027
articles.desc: Carbon composite woes cause another delay for Peter Beck's Hungry Hippo
articles.content: Rocket Lab pushes back first Neutron launch to 2027 Rocket Lab pushes back first Neutron launch to 2027 Carbon composite woes cause another delay for Peter Beck's Hungry Hippo SpaceX to buy key spectrum that could help Starlink Mobile become major US cell carrier Starlink's plan to avoid orbital near-misses: Ephemeris sharing Boeing's Calamity Capsule gets another shot at the ISS taxi business Starship finally makes orbit but engine trouble cuts the victory lap short SpaceX aims Starship for orbit on September 22 Rocket Lab has delayed the maiden launch of its Neutron rocket again, due to carbon composite manufacturing issues. It is more than five years since Rocket Lab it was developing the launcher, a step up from its workhorse Electron, and capable of sending up to 13,000 kg to Low Earth Orbit. At the time, 2024 was mooted as the first launch date. Then perhaps 2025. Then 2026. And now it is It won't be early in 2027 either. During a briefing, boss Peter Beck said he expects to complete testing of the problematic components before the end of Q1 2027, at which point it will set a new launch date. According to Beck, Rocket Lab identified problems with a first-stage tank that failed qualification due to third-party processing. The space biz switched to its own internal processes, and things appeared to be going swimmingly until, Beck said, "we identified an issue with the manufacturing process for the propellant dome." The issue was voids that formed within the carbon composite layers during manufacturing. Beck explained, "They don't necessarily mean that the dome would fail in flight," but they would reduce the margin, so a rethink was required. The good news, according to Beck, is that the problem is solved. The bad news? Dealing with it has delayed things. it targeted delivery of Neutron to the launch pad in Q4 2026. Beck now reckons the cryo and hydrostatic test campaigns will not wrap up until Q1 2027. Rocket Lab's shares have taken a battering following the announcement, dropping from about $63 yesterday to near $53 in after-hours trading. When it becomes operational, Neutron will feature an entirely reusable first stage with a "Hungry Hippo" clamshell fairing, opening to deploy a second stage before closing for a return to Earth. The timing of Neutron's availability is of note since it could come as SpaceX seeks to wind down Falcon 9 in favor of Starship. While Falcon 9 can loft heavier payloads, Neutron's mass capability puts it firmly in the same class. Speaking at the plenary session of the 7th CICA Summit in Baku, Azerbaijan, he expressed Bangladesh's support for transforming CICA into a fully fledged international regional organisation with clear legal status, a stronger secretariat, predictable financing and effective decision-making mechanisms, according to a ministry press release. During the summit, Laos became the 29th member of the pan-Asian forum, which was established in 1999 to promote peace, security and stability across Asia. The summit also endorsed Azerbaijan's chairmanship for 2026-28 and appointed Sultan Hajiyev as CICA's next secretary-general. articles.title: UzNIF Investor Day in Tashkent Attracts Over 200 Participants
articles.desc: Uzbekistan’s National Investment Fund and Franklin Templeton hosted UzNIF Investor Day 2026 in Tashkent, bringing together over 200 participants from global markets.
articles.content: UzNIF Investor Day in Tashkent Attracts Over 200 Participants — UzDaily.uz UzNIF Investor Day in Tashkent Attracts Over 200 Participants Uzbekistan’s National Investment Fund (UzNIF), together with its investment manager Franklin Templeton, held the second UzNIF Investor Day 2026 in Tashkent from 13 to 15 October. More than 200 people attended the event, including representatives of 60 global and regional asset management companies, Franklin Templeton said. Participants also included senior government officials, investment analysts, representatives of portfolio companies and business executives. Investors from North America, Europe, the Middle East and Asia explored investment opportunities in Uzbekistan and reviewed the transformation of companies in the fund’s portfolio. The three-day programme followed the fund’s share listing on the London Stock Exchange and the Toshkent Republican Stock Exchange in May 2026. The programme included site visits, presentations by government and central bank representatives, expert panels on key industries, and individual and group meetings with the management of the fund and its portfolio companies. The event began on 13 October with visits to key assets held by the fund. Participants toured the Charvak Hydropower Plant, the Kadirya Water Treatment Plant and Uzbekistan Airways’ aircraft maintenance and repair facility. The following day, government and industry representatives discussed the investment climate and opportunities in the energy, telecommunications and transport sectors. articles.content: Manulife launches AI assistant for advisor underwriting queries | Wealth Professional Manulife launches AI assistant for advisor underwriting queries Life, critical illness and Synergy covered first, with the AI tool drawing on Manulife handbooks Advisors selling Manulife life and critical illness policies can now put underwriting questions to an AI assistant at any hour and get answers pulled from the insurer’s underwriting advisor handbooks. is live through Advisor Portal, the company said in announcing the launch, and takes questions in plain language. The first release covers life insurance, critical illness insurance, and Synergy products. Manulife’s statement positions it before the application stage, where it helps advisors prepare for client conversations, understand potential underwriting requirements, and gather information earlier in the insurance process. MAUDE, the company’s AI-enabled underwriting engine, handles the stage after an application is submitted. Karen Cutler, chief underwriter at Manulife Canada, said in the announcement that advisors who reach the information they need faster can help clients act sooner. She said the Manulife Advisor AI Assistant provides underwriting guidance and sets up future tools for advisors. The assistant does not make underwriting decisions and does not provide a binding indication of insurability, premium, coverage, or application outcome. All applications remain subject to the insurer’s applicable underwriting requirements and evaluation. Manulife stated that advisors are expected to exercise professional judgment when using the tool, as AI-generated responses may contain errors. It operates within the company’s AI governance framework, covering risk management, human oversight, privacy safeguards, and ongoing monitoring. Jamie Campbell, head of artificial intelligence and data for Canada at Manulife, said in the announcement that the Manulife Advisor AI Assistant makes underwriting information “easier to find.” He said advisors can spend more time on their clients. Manulife expects to generate more than $1bn of by 2027 from becoming an AI-powered organisation, with $300m achieved as of year-end 2025. Evident named Manulife the number one life insurer for AI maturity for a second consecutive year earlier this year, per the same statement, which also cites Celent Model Insurer recognition for AI leadership in underwriting. articles.title: Kawasaki KLX300 XPL revealed
articles.desc: Now the KLX300 lineup has a total of four motorcycles.
articles.content: Kawasaki KLX300 XPL revealed | Autocar India Now the KLX300 lineup has a total of four motorcycles. Kawasaki has launched the KLX300 XPL in America, priced at USD 6,499 (equivalent to Rs 6.17 lakh). This travel-oriented dual-sport motorcycle is based on the base KLX300 but has factory-fitted accessories which include a tall windscreen, handguard and rear carrier. This lineup also comprises the standard KLX300, the KLX300 DF (which adds a hand guard and a rear carrier as standard), and KLX300 SM (supermoto with 17-inch wheels and road-focused tyres). Powered by a 292cc liquid-cooled engine making 27hp, 25Nm of torque Gets adjustable suspension both at the front and rear The liquid-cooled single-cylinder engine makes around 27hp and 25Nm of torque Setting the new KLX300 XPL apart from the rest of the range is a distinct round LED headlight. All four variants are powered by the 292cc liquid-cooled single-cylinder engine, producing 26.8hp at 8,000rpm and 24.9Nm of torque at 6,800rpm, paired with a 6-speed gearbox. Kawasaki has introduced revised internals like a new connecting rod bearing design across the 2027 range to enhance engine performance and reliability. The twin-radiator setup from the previous model has also given way to a repositioned single unit to accommodate the new ABS hardware. On the features front, the 2027 updates brings a redesigned LCD instrument cluster with smartphone connectivity through the Kawasaki Rideology app. Kawasaki has also equipped the KLX300 lineup with front-wheel ABS, which can be disabled to tailor braking performance when riding off-road. When the motorcycle is turned off and restarted, ABS automatically returns to its default active setting. Chassis setup comprises a double cradle frame paired with an aluminum swingarm. Up front, it features a 43mm USD fork with adjustable compression damping, while the rear gets a fully adjustable link-type monoshock. Despite the additional equipment on offer, the KLX300 XPL (142kg) only weighs 3kg more than the KLX230 which is sold in India (139kg). In theory, the KLX300 would make for a good step up from the KLX230 (Rs 2.19 lakh ex-showroom) sold in India, which has an air-cooled 233cc motor. However, Kawasaki India currently has made no announcement to indicate that the liquid-cooled KLX models will be coming to our shores. articles.title: Check Market Structure to Avoid Round Number Traps
articles.desc: Explain the Concept Psychological levels often form around round numbers because human beings tend to think in whole figures for simplicity. When market participants set targets, entries, or protective stops, they frequently choose prices ending in zero. This shared habit causes buy and sell orders
articles.content: Explain the Concept Psychological levels often form around round numbers because human beings tend to think in whole figures for simplicity. When market participants set targets, entries, or protective stops, they frequently choose prices ending in zero. This shared habit causes buy and sell orders to cluster at these precise points, which can temporarily alter supply and demand dynamics when the price approaches them. Identify What to Observe Observe how price behaviour at a psychological round number differs from its behaviour at a proven structural level. Reactions at round numbers can often be brief or volatile, driven by the immediate triggering of clustered orders. In contrast, reactions at true structural levels, which are backed by historical trading activity or volume accumulation, tend to represent more significant and sustained shifts in market interest. Show How to Check It We can examine this distinction on the current 4-hour chart for NSE:NIFTY, where the price is presently at 22939. The Average True Range (ATR) over 14 periods is 221, meaning the average movement of one 4-hour candle is 0.96 percent. While the current price is near a major round psychological level, the actual structural zone of interest rests higher at 23241 to 23501. This area is the largest time-price profile ledge, holding 13 percent of the profile, and is confirmed by historical chart extremes. Working from this validated zone provides a clearer technical framework than acting on round numbers alone. When mapping a scenario from this specific zone of interest, structural supports define the objectives. Target 1 is established at 22687, supported by a 5.3 percent time-price ledge and a recent swing, representing a move of 2.5 ATR or 2.4 percent from the zone. Target 2 is 22180, which aligns precisely with the extreme of a 260-bar window, marking a move of 4.8 ATR or 4.6 percent. Target 3 is 21524, based on a 161.8 percent projection, translating to a 7.8 ATR or 7.4 percent move from the zone. The technical invalidation level sits at 23426, just beyond the far boundary of the resistance zone, which structures the risk to the first target at a ratio of 1 to 3.0. Name a Common Mistake A frequent error is using a round number as the only justification for entering a trade or placing a stop order. Because automated algorithms are aware of order clustering at round numbers, these areas are often deliberately breached to collect liquidity, leading to false breakouts before the market reverses. Risk-Aware Practice Step As a practice exercise, scan your charts to locate robust structural zones first, relying on volume ledges and historical chart extremes. Once your primary zones and technical invalidation points are established based on pure data, you can note if any round numbers fall near your structural targets to act as secondary confluence. Always prioritize actual market structure over psychological price points to manage risk effectively.

articles.title: Jackie the Bald Eagle's Cause of Death Revealed: Bird Flu Triggered Severe Stomach Ulcer and Internal Bleeding
articles.desc: Jackie the bald eagle died from complications of bird flu, which caused a severe stomach ulcer, internal bleeding, anemia and bacterial sepsis, wildlife officials confirmed.
articles.content: Jackie the Bald Eagle's Cause of Death Revealed: Bird Flu Trig... Jackie the Bald Eagle's Cause of Death Revealed: Bird Flu Triggered Severe Stomach Ulcer and Internal Bleeding Necropsy findings identified highly pathogenic avian influenza as the primary cause of death, while tests found no evidence that her mate, Shadow, or their eaglets were sick. Jackie, the beloved bald eagle watched by millions through a livestream from Big Bear Lake in Southern California, died in August after bird flu caused a severe stomach ulcer, ongoing internal bleeding, and a dangerous bacterial infection, wildlife officials revealed on Wednesday, Oct. 14, 2026. A necropsy, or animal autopsy, and additional laboratory tests identified highly pathogenic avian influenza (HPAI) as the primary underlying cause of her decline. The findings come nearly two months after the roughly 14-year-old eagle died following weeks of treatment at the Ojai Raptor Center. The results explain why Jackie continued to deteriorate despite intensive veterinary care, including a blood transfusion. They also show that her illness involved several connected medical problems, although officials say there is no evidence that her mate, Shadow, or their eaglets are sick. How Bird Flu Caused Jackie's Fatal Illness According to the California Department of Fish and Wildlife, the bird flu infection caused an unusual form of disease in Jackie. It led to a severe ulcer in the muscular part of her stomach, known as the ventriculus or gizzard. The damaged tissue caused persistent internal bleeding, which resulted in severe anemia, a condition in which the body does not have enough healthy red blood cells to carry oxygen. The ulcer also allowed bacteria to enter her body, leading to sepsis, a serious reaction to infection that can damage organs. Steve Kubiski, director of disease investigations at the San Diego Zoo Wildlife Alliance, which performed the necropsy, explained the findings. "In an uncommon presentation of the virus, the infection caused a severe ulcer in her stomach that led to persistent internal bleeding, anemia, and the development of bacterial sepsis," Kubiski said. Wildlife officials also found severe inflammation and blood clots in Jackie's heart and several major blood vessels. Tests detected genetic material from the bird flu virus in multiple tissues, including the ulcerated stomach tissue. The findings help explain why her condition remained difficult to treat during her final weeks. What Other Tests Revealed About Jackie's Health The examination also investigated whether other infections or toxic substances contributed to Jackie's death. Testing showed that she was negative for West Nile virus, while heavy metal levels in her body were within acceptable limits. However, toxicology screening detected brodifacoum, an anticoagulant rodenticide commonly used in rat poison, in her liver. Brodifacoum can interfere with blood clotting, but the necropsy did not identify the uncontrolled bleeding typically associated with the chemical. Officials therefore did not consider it the primary cause of her illness or death. The California Department of Fish and Wildlife said the results pointed to several serious health problems developing together over time. Bird flu was identified as the primary underlying cause. Chris Eksteen, executive director of the Ojai Raptor Center, which cared for Jackie after her rescue, said the findings helped explain what veterinarians observed during her treatment. "The necropsy results have helped connect many of the findings we were seeing throughout the eagle's hospitalization," Eksteen said. He added that the team was grateful to the veterinary specialists, laboratories, wildlife agencies and partner organizations that helped investigate her illness and provide care. "Caring for her was an extraordinary privilege for our entire team," he said. From a Dramatic Rescue to Weeks of Treatment Jackie was rescued in July after she was seen fighting wi

articles.title: Library exhibit highlights endangered languages
articles.desc: An exhibit of Cornell research, teaching, and collections highlight the work of revitalizing endangered languages.
articles.content: Library exhibit highlights endangered languages | Cornell Chronicle News directly from Cornell's colleges and centers What factors can cause languages to disappear over time, and what can communities do to keep their languages alive? A new exhibit by Cornell University Library and the Department of Linguistics answers these questions by using examples of Cornell collections, teaching, and research on endangered languages. Languages at the Brink: Threatened Languages and How We Protect Them opens at the Kroch Library on October 22, with 4:30-6:00 p.m. in Olin Library 107. The reception will feature a presentation by , professor of linguistics at Cornell, who will share his experiences teaching the Introduction to Language Endangerment and Revitalization class. He will be joined by his students, who will talk about their research projects for the class that are included in the exhibit. The exhibit focuses on five examples of endangered languages: the Ainu language of northern Japan; the Celtic language Welsh; Yiddish, a Germanic language with elements of Slavic and Hebrew; Garifuna, a Caribbean Arawakan language with West African influence; and Gayogo̱hó:nǫ , the Indigenous language of the region where Cornell University is located. provides brief histories of these languages and highlights current revitalization efforts at Cornell and elsewhere, while featuring materials from Cornell University Library’s collections. “Our collections include items that are in over 460 languages, and we have many scholarly materials related to the study of endangered languages,” said Phil Robinson M.A. ’13, assistant director of software development and linguistics selector for Cornell University Library who co-curated the exhibit with Whitman. “We’re displaying images, books, and audio pertaining to communities who are striving to protect and revive their endangered languages in the face of colonialization and other challenges.” is a special case in point, according to Whitman. “Cornell is the only Ivy League university that is teaching the indigenous language of its region,” he said. Whitman praised the library for its related collections and the integral pedagogical work of Stephen Henhawk, a first-language speaker of Gayogo̱hó:nǫ Robinson and Whitman emphasized that community engagement, above all else, is the key to language survival. “The most important work that an institution like Cornell can do is to assist communities that really are committed to keeping their language alive when it’s endangered,” said Whitman, who prefers the term “language reclamation” over “language revitalization” to describe the endeavor. “‘Reclamation’ clearly states that it is the people who have the language who are reclaiming it, who are getting it back, and that point is truly important,” Whitman said. “Languages at the Brink: Threatened Languages and How We Protect Them” runs through May 2027. It is the final installment of a series of exhibits titled “From the Brink: Contributions to a Sustainable Future from across Cornell,” hosted by unit libraries of Cornell University Library in partnership with departments and groups on campus. Jose Beduya is a writer and editor for Cornell University Library. Get Cornell news delivered right to your inbox.
